@graph.headline: Proof, Not Promises: Three Metro Detroit Modernizations and What You Can Verify Yourself
@graph.description: Three anonymized engagements — a website build, a local LLM deployment, and a Chainlink-verified workflow — each ending in an artifact the client holds, not a dashboard the vendor owns. Plus the five questions that separate a real case study from a testimonial.

about.name: Metro Detroit business modernization case studies — three anonymized engagements across the three Agentic service lines: a professional website build for an established contractor stuck on a single landing page (page architecture, indexation, owned analytics), a local LLM device deployment for a law firm that had banned cloud AI (retrieval scope, prompt library, evaluation set, network egress evidence), and a Chainlink Runtime Environment (CRE) workflow connecting three counterparties through consensus-verified attestations (hashed records, dispute resolution, exception handling). Includes the shared success factors across engagements, a five-question test for reading any vendor case study, and explicit limits.

mainEntity.name: What does a modernization engagement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Website builds are scoped by page count and complexity; local LLM deployments by device tier and workload, where a capable desktop device runs roughly $4,700 to $5,500 plus support; CRE work by counterparties and exception volume. All three are quoted after a diagnosis, not before.

mainEntity.name: How long before we see anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six weeks for a website build, five for a single local LLM deployment including its evaluation set, nine for a multi-party verified workflow. The first visible change usually arrives sooner: the day the baseline gets measured.

mainEntity.name: Do you publish named client case studies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rarely. Practices and healthcare clients will not attach a name to a piece describing their internal systems, and asking damages the relationship. The trade is verification instead — artifacts a client can show, references off the record, and numbers the client publishes if they choose.

mainEntity.name: We have all three problems. What do we fix first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whichever is losing money today. If prospects cannot find or believe you, the website is the bottleneck. If staff already use consumer AI on client data, the exposure is the bottleneck and the only one with a legal clock on it — HIPAA-ready AI is a design constraint, not a badge. Workflow verification usually comes third, because it depends on the other two being defined.

mainEntity.name: How do we check a vendor's claims before we hire?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for the artifact, the baseline, and the account holding the measurement. Then ask what failed. A vendor who answers all three in one meeting is describing work they did; one who cannot is describing work they would like to do.
